evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructure and properties of sintered the Mo-Re-ZrO2
evidence.quote: Fig. 5 (a, c) shows the initial microstructures of the two alloys exhibit a comparatively random grain orientation and the grains are similar in size to each other, which resemble the equiaxed crystal structure. The grain size of the Mo-5 %Re alloy is significantly refined after the addition of the ZrO2 particles. Fig. 5 b shows the grain size distribution of Mo-Re alloy with an average particle size of 14.99 μm.

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructure and properties of sintered the Mo-Re-ZrO2
evidence.quote: The grain refinement due to the increased contact area between the liquid particles during the liquid phase doping process, and the ZrO2 particles can be more evenly and densely distributed inside the Mo-Re matrix grains, which prevents the tendency of particles to grow during subsequent reduction and high temperature sintering processes and inhibits grain growth.

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructure and properties of sintered the Mo-Re-ZrO2
evidence.quote: The movement of ZrO2 particles and the matrix in the semi-coherent interface restricts each other, which can significantly refine the grain size and inhibit the growth of the second phase particles. The finer the ZrO2 particles, the stronger the pinning effect on dislocations, and the higher the strength of the alloy.

evidence.section: 3.6.3 Texture evolution
evidence.quote: When the Mo-Re-ZrO2 alloy is deformed at 1100 ℃, the recrystallization area is large and the proportion of dynamic recrystallization is high, which indicates that ZrO2 promotes the occurrence of dynamic recrystallization as a nucleation particle during thermal deformation process. When the temperature rises to 1400 ℃, the dynamic recrystallization rate of Mo-Re-ZrO2 alloy is lower than that of Mo-Re alloy, because the fine dispersed ZrO2 particles exert significance Zener-drag effects, which delays the occurrence of dynamic recrystallization.
